text:
Devon: heads-up — ~12% GPU capacity drop in us-west3 starting ~08:02 UTC. Seeing ECC counts climbing and bursts of Xid errors across racks r12-r14. Telemetry also shows intermittent BMC timeouts. Anyone oncall?
Maria: on it, pulling node logs now. Which pools are affected?
Devon: prod-infer and some batch-train. Prod-infer is taking the brunt. Scheduler started aggressive backfills which is thrashing QoS.
Kyle: quick sample from /var/log/gpu-monitor that started at 08:03:
```
[08:03:12] host-r12-0 GPU0 ecc_uncorrectable=1345
[08:03:13] host-r12-0 GPU1 Xid=61 timeout
[08:03:13] host-r13-2 BMC: timeout on mgmt bus
```
Maria: I see the same pattern on r12-14. Rate of uncorrectable ECCs is unusual (sustained).
Jen: I've tagged host-r12-0, host-r12-1, host-r13-2, host-r14-3 as hardware-flaky and started drains. Kicking long-running jobs off those GPUs now.
sre-bot: Drains initiated for 7 hosts (r12-r14). Est. immediate impact: 9% capacity loss. Runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/gpu-drain-procedure
Maria: draining pushed backfill into us-west2 spots — autoscaler spun up ephemeral instances. Cost risk rising.
Devon: pause autoscaler for prod-infer and prefer dedicated pools while we triage. We can't let spot churn hit latency SLOs.
Kyle: applying temporary scheduler policy: prefer_dedicated=100 for pool prod-infer, duration=15m. Doing now.
Kyle: policy applied. Autoscaler paused for prod-infer.
Maria: correlating telemetry — BMC timeouts and NIC CRC errors on the same hosts. Looks like a firmware regression after last BIOS/KCS push last week.
Jen: Ops action: schedule hardware replacement for nodes with repeated BMC timeouts. Also propose rolling firmware rollback for affected rack if vendor supports it.
Devon: create an incident and notify support + customers impacted. @sre-bot please create incident 'usw3-gpu-flakiness' and assign Sev2.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-202403-21 (Sev2) — channels: #incidents, #eng-runtime, #support.
Kyle: quick mitigation thought — marking GPUs as do-not-schedule and enabling model-fallback to smaller variants for prod-infer. Less compute per request but keeps latency.
Maria: doing that now: added do-not-schedule tag to 7 GPUs and bumped fallback routing for critical routes. Also increased KV cache TTL to reduce token generation pressure.
Jen: scheduling replacement window tomorrow 02:00-06:00 UTC for racks r12-r14. Need approval from infra procurement for accelerated RMAs.
Devon: note on cost — autoscaler spin-up during backfill cost ~ $2k in ephemeral spot GPUs in the last 40m. We'll attach to the incident and chargeback to infra/test.
Maria: root-cause hypothesis for now: firmware regression interacting with mgmt NIC driver causing BMC hangs, leading to GPU ECC flakiness under load.
Devon: good. Owner for postmortem is me (Devon). Please paste any logs or probes into INC-202403-21. We'll coordinate with vendor and schedule firmware rollback if safe.
Kyle: also collecting kernel oops and dmesg snapshots from the affected hosts to send to vendor.
Jen: ops will start procurement for hot-swap replacements and prepare handoff doc.
Devon: I'll draft customer comms for impacted tenants and note degraded capacity + mitigation steps. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
